title: From Tool Traces to Strategy Banks: Mining Failure Signatures for Budgeted Repository-Level Code Repair

problem.claim: Repository-level code repair produces rich tool traces, but most LLM agents discard them and repeatedly restart from a fixed debugging loop.

gap.claim: Existing debugging loops do not reuse mined information from prior tool traces to guide repair under task constraints.

contributions.claim: Evolutionary Self-Debugging Agents mine tool traces into structured failure signatures and maintain a reusable strategy bank of debugging policies.
The strategy bank stores policies as modular prompt genomes with typed slots that support slot-level reuse, mutation, and crossover.
A cost-aware ranking objective prioritizes strategies likely to succeed within the first few evaluator calls under tight budgets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On RepoBench, ESDA solves 58.4% of tasks within the first two evaluator calls.
On RepoBench, ESDA reduces median wall-clock time by 3.0x compared with strong baselines.
The authors report consistent gains from mining failure signatures when transferring across languages and build systems under distribution shift.

narrative_sequence.summary: Repository-level repair generates useful tool traces that LLM agents generally discard while repeating a fixed debugging loop.
ESDA converts tool traces into failure signatures and maintains reusable debugging policies in a strategy bank.
Policies use modular prompt genomes with typed slots for reuse, mutation, and crossover.
Cost-aware ranking favors strategies expected to succeed within the first few evaluator calls under limited budgets.
The authors report improved early-call success, lower median wall-clock time, and consistent transfer gains under distribution shift.

source_observation.claim: Mining failure signatures from tool traces is associated with higher early-call repair success and faster median completion in the reported RepoBench evaluation.

interpretation.claim: Structured reuse of observed failure patterns may be more effective than restarting a fixed debugging loop for budget-constrained repair.

application.claim: A repair system could retain typed, modular strategy components and rank them by expected success within the available evaluator-call budget.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that the reported gains generalize beyond the stated RepoBench setting or the examined language and build-system shifts.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the baseline identities or evaluation protocol details.
The abstract does not describe the failure-signature schema or ranking objective formulation.
The abstract does not report per-language or per-build-system results.
